stimuli.title: Case study: Larkspur Freight
stimuli.text:
**Company overview.** Larkspur Freight is a fictional road and rail logistics company with depots in Europe and North America. It runs its systems in two leased data centers, and the European lease ends in 18 months.

**Solution concept.** Larkspur wants to move its systems to Google Cloud, stream telemetry from 9,000 trucks for live tracking and late-delivery prediction, and give dispatchers a generative AI assistant that answers questions from the company's own operating manuals.

**Existing technical environment.**
- Java order and dispatch applications on about 300 VMs, with a MySQL database for orders.
- A nightly Hadoop and Spark batch that builds delivery reports.
- Trucks send GPS and engine readings every 30 seconds to an on-premises message queue.
- A licensed commercial database for invoicing, licensed per physical core.

**Business requirements.**
- Leave the European data center before the lease ends, with little change to applications in the first phase.
- Personal data about European customers and drivers must stay in the EU.
- Cut the time from a delay to a customer alert from hours to minutes.

**Technical requirements.**
- Order processing must keep running if one zone fails.
- Telemetry spikes at the start of each shift must not drop messages.
- The dispatcher assistant must answer only from approved manuals and cite them.

**Executive statement.** "We are a logistics company, not a data center company. Move first, then make it better."

stimuli.title: Case study: Pinecrest Clinics
stimuli.text:
**Company overview.** Pinecrest Clinics is a fictional network of 60 outpatient clinics in the United States. It stores protected health information and must comply with HIPAA.

**Solution concept.** Pinecrest is building a patient app for booking and test results, moving its imaging archive off tape, and using generative AI to draft summaries of call-center conversations for staff to review.

**Existing technical environment.**
- An electronic records vendor system on premises, which exposes HL7 and FHIR interfaces.
- A PostgreSQL booking database and a web front end on VMs.
- Medical images on tape libraries, rarely read after the first year but kept for many years.
- One central IT team. Clinic staff sign in with the company's existing identity provider.

**Business requirements.**
- Patients must be able to book from a phone, including during flu season peaks.
- Developers must never see real patient data in test environments.
- Auditors must be able to see who read patient records.

**Technical requirements.**
- Patient data must not leave a defined service perimeter, even if a credential is stolen.
- The company wants to hold its own encryption keys for patient data.
- Call transcripts sent to a model must be screened for sensitive data first.

**Executive statement.** "Patients trust us with their records. Every design choice starts there."

stimuli.title: Case study: Brightwave Learning
stimuli.text:
**Company overview.** Brightwave Learning is a fictional online learning company that sells video courses and practice quizzes to schools and families in North America, Europe and Asia. Some of its users are under 13.

**Solution concept.** Brightwave wants an AI study tutor that explains quiz answers, faster video delivery worldwide, and a platform its 12 product teams can deploy to every day without waiting on operations.

**Existing technical environment.**
- A monolithic Python web application already running on Compute Engine in one US region.
- Course videos in Cloud Storage, served from that region.
- A Cloud SQL for MySQL database that is near its limits during exam weeks.
- Releases are manual, monthly and often rolled back.

**Business requirements.**
- Traffic grows about tenfold in the two weeks before school exams.
- Parental consent and data rules for children must be met in every country it serves.
- Teams want to release features independently.

**Technical requirements.**
- Learners anywhere should see low latency for pages and videos.
- The tutor must refuse off-topic or unsafe requests and must not reveal other learners' data.
- Cost must fall back after each exam season.

**Executive statement.** "Our best weeks are the weeks our site is slowest. That has to end."

stimuli.title: Case study: Harborline Bank
stimuli.text:
**Company overview.** Harborline Bank is a fictional regional bank with card payments, savings and loans. It must comply with PCI DSS for card data and with banking regulators who audit its controls.

**Solution concept.** Harborline wants to close one of its two data centers, score card payments for fraud in real time, and give relationship managers a generative AI assistant that drafts client briefings.

**Existing technical environment.**
- About 1,200 VMs on VMware vSphere, many running vendor software that is supported only on VMware.
- A card-authorization system that must answer within strict latency limits.
- Nightly batch jobs that settle payments and feed a data warehouse.
- Separate teams run networks, security and applications.

**Business requirements.**
- Close the first data center within a year without rewriting vendor applications.
- Prove to auditors that no single administrator can both change and approve production access.
- Keep card data in a clearly scoped environment.

**Technical requirements.**
- Private, high-bandwidth connectivity between the remaining data center and Google Cloud.
- Fraud scoring must take the most recent transactions into account.
- Every infrastructure change must be reviewed and reproducible.

**Executive statement.** "Regulators will judge us on control, not speed. We want both."

questions.stem: A team of analysts needs to run queries in BigQuery in one project but must not change datasets or IAM. What is the best way to grant access?
options: Grant the basic Editor role to each analyst on the project
Grant a predefined BigQuery role to their group
Grant the basic Owner role to the group so nobody is blocked
One shared service account key
questions.explanation: Predefined roles grant only the permissions a job function needs, and granting them to a group makes access easy to manage as people join and leave. Basic roles such as Editor and Owner are far too broad, and a shared key removes individual accountability.

questions.stem: Developers merge code once a month and spend days fixing conflicts and broken builds. Which practice addresses this most directly?
options: Let a single engineer merge every change by hand at the month's end
Merge small changes often, each built and tested
Ask developers to merge even less often so there are fewer merges
Skip tests so builds are faster
questions.explanation: Continuous integration means merging small changes frequently, with each merge built and tested automatically, so problems appear while they are small and easy to fix. Merging less often, or manually, makes conflicts larger.

questions.stem: Partners call an Apigee proxy for product details thousands of times a minute, the answers change only hourly, and the legacy back end is struggling. Which Apigee capability helps most?
options: A response cache policy on the proxy
OAuth token checks on every request
A Spike Arrest policy set very low
A new developer portal for partners
questions.explanation: A ResponseCache policy stores responses in Apigee for a set time, so repeated identical requests are answered without calling the back end. Spike Arrest would protect the back end by rejecting partner calls, and a portal or OAuth checks do not reduce back-end load.

questions.stem: A Bigtable table stores readings from 50,000 sensors, and its row key starts with the reading's timestamp. Writes pile up on one node while others sit idle. What should the architect change?
options: Switch the table to Cloud SQL with a time index
Move the timestamp into a separate column family
Add more nodes so each one takes a share of writes
Start the row key with the sensor ID, then the time
questions.explanation: Row keys that start with a timestamp send every new write to the end of the key range, so one node takes all the load. Leading with a well-distributed value such as the sensor ID spreads writes across nodes while keeping each sensor's readings together. Adding nodes does not help when all writes target one key range.

questions.stem: A team says its API "should be fast." How should an SRE-minded architect turn this into something the team can operate against?
options: Promise customers that the API will never have any slow requests
Define a latency SLI and set an SLO target for it
Ask users if it feels fast
Add more servers whenever someone on the team feels it is slow
questions.explanation: A service level indicator measures behavior, such as the share of requests served under a latency threshold, and a service level objective sets the target for it over a period. That gives an error budget and objective alerts; feelings and promises of perfection do not.

questions.stem: A product owner writes: "Customers can download their invoices as PDF" and "Invoice pages load in under two seconds for 95% of requests." How should an architect classify these?
options: The first is functional and the second is non-functional
Both are functional, because each describes a user story
The first is non-functional and the second is functional
Both are non-functional, because each can be measured in a test
questions.explanation: A functional requirement says what the system does (download invoices). A non-functional requirement sets a quality target such as latency, availability or security. Latency targets are a classic non-functional requirement that drives the choice of caching, region and database.

questions.stem: VMs with no external IP addresses must read objects from Cloud Storage. What should be enabled on their subnet?
options: Private Google Access
Cloud Armor
Cloud CDN
Alias IP ranges on the subnet
questions.explanation: Private Google Access lets VMs with only internal IP addresses reach Google APIs and services such as Cloud Storage. Cloud CDN caches content for users, Cloud Armor filters inbound web traffic, and alias IPs give extra addresses to a VM.

questions.stem: A company wants every project in its production business units to inherit the same security policies, while sandbox projects get looser ones. How should the hierarchy be designed?
options: Production and sandbox folders, with policies on each
One project for the whole company, with labels marking production resources
Projects under the organization, set by hand
A separate organization for each team, with no shared policies between them
questions.explanation: Policies set on a folder are inherited by every project beneath it, so grouping projects into production and sandbox folders applies the right controls automatically. Labels do not carry IAM or organization policies, and many organizations or hand-configured projects lose central control.

questions.stem: An internal reporting tool can be down for a day after a regional disaster, and the business wants the lowest DR cost. Which pattern fits?
options: Cold standby: back up and rebuild in another region
Hot standby: a full copy running in another region at all times
Active-active: serve users from two regions at the same time
Warm standby in a second region
questions.explanation: A generous recovery time objective allows a cold pattern, where backups and infrastructure as code are ready but nothing runs until a disaster, which costs least. Warm, hot and active-active patterns cut recovery time at a higher ongoing cost.

questions.stem: Developers want to run integration tests against Pub/Sub on their laptops without creating real cloud resources or costs. What should they use?
options: The Pub/Sub emulator started with gcloud
A Cloud SQL database instead of Pub/Sub
A production Pub/Sub topic shared by all developers
A Cloud Storage bucket used as a message queue
questions.explanation: Google Cloud provides local emulators for Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Spanner and Firestore that start from the gcloud CLI, so tests run locally with no cloud cost or shared state. Using production resources for tests risks data and interference.

questions.stem: Several product teams each have their own project, and a central network team must control subnets, routes and firewall rules for all of them. Which design fits?
options: Shared VPC with a host project and service projects
One project holding every team's resources together
A separate VPC in each project joined by VPC peering
Cloud VPN tunnels between each pair of team projects
questions.explanation: Shared VPC lets a host project own the network while service projects attach their resources to its subnets, so one team controls networking and the product teams keep their own projects, billing and IAM. Peering many VPCs spreads network control across teams and is not transitive.

questions.stem: A data science team retrains a model by hand each month: it pulls data, trains, evaluates and deploys, and steps are sometimes skipped. What should the architect recommend?
options: Write the steps in a shared document for each person to follow
Train the model once and never retrain it after that
Run each step from a different person's laptop to share work
Automate the steps as an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow
questions.explanation: Agent Platform Pipelines (formerly Vertex AI Pipelines) runs the ML lifecycle as a repeatable, versioned workflow with tracked inputs and outputs, so no step is skipped and each run can be audited. A checklist is still manual, and never retraining lets the model drift as data changes.

questions.stem: An on-call team gets dozens of alerts a night for brief CPU spikes that never affect users, and real incidents get missed. What should change?
options: Add more CPU alerts with lower thresholds on every VM
Alert on user-facing symptoms such as SLO burn rate instead
Turn off all alerting and check the dashboards each morning
Send every alert to the whole company so someone responds
questions.explanation: Good alerting pages people for symptoms that affect users, such as an error budget burning too fast, and leaves causes like brief CPU spikes to dashboards. Noisy alerts cause fatigue and missed incidents; removing alerts entirely hides real problems.

questions.stem: A company has a 15-year-old in-house HR system that a SaaS product now does better and that no team wants to maintain. Which disposition fits it best in the migration plan?
options: Keep it on premises for now
Replace it with the SaaS product
Refactor it into microservices on GKE first
Rehost it on Compute Engine as it is today
questions.explanation: When a commercial product already covers the need and the custom system has no owner, buying and retiring is cheaper than moving or rewriting it. Rehosting carries the maintenance burden forward, and refactoring spends engineering time on a system the business does not want to own.

questions.stem: Regulators require trade records in a bucket to be kept unchanged for seven years, and even administrators must not be able to delete them early. What should the architect configure?
options: An IAM role that only lets admins delete objects
A bucket retention policy locked with Bucket Lock
A lifecycle rule moving objects to Archive storage
Object Versioning with no lifecycle rules
questions.explanation: A retention policy stops objects being deleted or overwritten until they reach the set age, and locking it with Bucket Lock makes the policy permanent so nobody can shorten or remove it. Versioning keeps old copies but deletions are still possible, and storage classes change cost, not protection.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. Which requirement should drive the order-processing tier's deployment design first?
options: Delay alerts must reach customers in minutes, not hours
Order processing must keep running if one zone fails
Telemetry spikes at shift start must not drop messages
The assistant must answer only from approved manuals
questions.explanation: For the order tier, the stated availability requirement is zone failure tolerance, which points to multi-zone instance groups and a regional database. The other requirements belong to the telemetry pipeline and the assistant, which are separate parts of the design.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. How should the architect host the invoicing database so the company can keep using its existing per-physical-core licenses?
options: On sole-tenant nodes with dedicated physical cores
On Spot VMs, so licensed cores cost less to run
On shared-core VMs, so fewer physical cores are used
On Cloud Run, so the database runs only on request
questions.explanation: Bring-your-own-license terms that count physical cores usually need dedicated hardware. Sole-tenant nodes give the project physical servers of its own, so cores can be counted and kept constant. Shared or preemptible capacity cannot show which physical cores the software used.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. How should the architect configure ingestion so telemetry spikes at shift start do not drop messages?
options: Write telemetry straight into Cloud SQL from each truck at all times
Batch telemetry on each truck and upload a file once every night
Publish telemetry to Pub/Sub and process it with streaming Dataflow
Send telemetry to a single VM that writes it to a local disk file
questions.explanation: Pub/Sub absorbs bursts and retains unacknowledged messages, and streaming Dataflow scales its workers with the backlog, so spikes are buffered rather than lost. Writing directly to a relational database or a single VM creates a bottleneck, and nightly uploads break the minutes-level alerting requirement.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. How should the dispatcher assistant be designed to meet its technical requirement?
options: Fine-tune a model on public web pages about logistics and road freight
Answer from training data with a disclaimer
Give dispatchers a raw model endpoint and train them to check answers
Ground a Gemini model on the manuals, with citations
questions.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds the model's answers in the company's own approved documents and can return the source passages as citations, which is exactly the requirement. Fine-tuning on public data or answering from general training data does not limit answers to the manuals.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. How can the architect make sure personal data about European customers and drivers is only ever stored in the EU?
options: Store the data in a multi-region US bucket with customer-managed keys
A resource locations organization policy set to the EU
An eu label on each resource
Ask each developer to choose an EU region whenever they create resources
questions.explanation: The resource locations organization policy constraint restricts where location-based resources can be created, so projects holding EU personal data cannot use regions outside the EU. Labels and developer habits are not enforced, and keys do not change where data is stored. Assured Workloads can add further data residency controls.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. The CTO asks whether to refactor the Java apps into microservices before leaving the European data center. What should the architect advise?
options: Rewrite every app as Cloud Run functions before any of them can move
Rehost to meet the lease date, then modernize later
Renew the lease for ten years
Refactor everything first, even if the move misses the lease deadline
questions.explanation: The business requirements set a hard deadline and ask for little application change in the first phase, and the executive says "move first, then make it better." Rehosting now and modernizing afterward fits; a full refactor risks the lease date.

questions.stem: Refer to the Larkspur Freight case study. Which signal should operations watch to see early that delay alerts are falling behind real time?
options: The age of the oldest unacknowledged message in Pub/Sub
IAM roles in the telemetry project
The CPU use of the order database during the nightly batch
The total storage used by the company's Cloud Storage buckets
questions.explanation: If the oldest unacknowledged message is getting older, the pipeline is not keeping up and alerts will arrive late, which threatens the minutes-level requirement. Alerting on that age, along with Dataflow system lag, catches a backlog before customers notice.

questions.stem: A CI system running outside Google Cloud must deploy to a project, and the security team forbids long-lived service account keys. What should the architect use?
options: A service account key stored as a secret variable in the CI system
Owner for allUsers while deploying
Workload Identity Federation with the CI's tokens
A personal user account whose password is saved in the CI system
questions.explanation: Workload Identity Federation lets external workloads exchange their own identity tokens, such as OIDC tokens from a CI provider, for short-lived Google credentials to impersonate a service account, so no key file exists to leak. Stored keys or passwords are long-lived secrets, and granting to allUsers is public access.

questions.stem: After an outage caused by a bad configuration push, what should the team's postmortem focus on?
options: Rolling back every change made by the team in the last quarter
Causes and fixes to stop a repeat, without blame
Finding the engineer responsible so they can be held to account
A note that the outage is over
questions.explanation: A blameless postmortem records the timeline, impact, contributing causes and concrete follow-up actions, such as safer rollout and validation of configs. Blame discourages people from reporting what really happened, and reverting unrelated work does not fix the cause.

questions.stem: Several engineers run Terraform against the same environment and sometimes overwrite each other's changes. What should the architect recommend?
options: Commit the state file to Git after every change by hand
Store state in a remote Cloud Storage backend with locking
Stop using Terraform and make changes in the console
Keep a separate local state file on each engineer's laptop
questions.explanation: A shared remote backend such as a Cloud Storage bucket keeps one source of truth for Terraform state and locks it while an apply runs, so two runs cannot collide. Local state files drift apart, and state committed to Git can leak secrets and still conflicts.

questions.stem: A rendering job runs for hours across hundreds of VMs, checkpoints its progress, and can restart any frame that is lost. Which compute option cuts cost the most?
options: Standard VMs with a three-year commitment
Spot VMs in a managed instance group
A single large memory-optimized VM
Sole-tenant nodes with large machine types
questions.explanation: Spot VMs cost much less than standard VMs but can be stopped at any time, which a fault-tolerant, checkpointing batch can absorb. Commitments suit steady long-term use, and sole-tenant nodes are for licensing or isolation needs.

questions.stem: A service's CPU cost rose after a release, and the team wants to see which functions use the most CPU in production with low overhead. Which tool fits?
options: Cloud NAT logging
Cloud Profiler
Cloud DNS logging
Cloud Shell
questions.explanation: Cloud Profiler continuously samples CPU and memory use of running applications in production with low overhead and shows which functions consume the most. Cloud Trace shows request latency across services, and the others are not observability tools.

questions.stem: An application needs a third-party API key at runtime. Where should the key be kept?
options: A plain text file in a public Cloud Storage bucket
Hard-coded in the source code in the repository
An environment variable written into the container image
Secret Manager, read by the app's service account
questions.explanation: Secret Manager stores secrets with versioning, IAM access control and audit logging, and the application reads them at runtime with its own identity. Secrets in source code, images or public buckets can be copied by anyone who sees them.

questions.stem: An order service must survive the loss of a zone, and the business also wants the lowest cost. Which design meets the availability need with the least extra spend?
options: A zonal managed instance group with autohealing enabled
A regional managed instance group in two zones
Two instance groups in two regions
A single large VM with a snapshot schedule every hour
questions.explanation: A regional managed instance group spreads VMs across zones in one region, so a zone outage leaves capacity running. Snapshots and autohealing do not help when the whole zone is down, and a second region adds cost and complexity the requirement does not ask for.

questions.stem: A Cloud Run service must connect to a Memorystore instance that has only a private IP in a VPC network. What should the architect configure on the service?
options: An external passthrough Network Load Balancer
Direct VPC egress to the VPC network
A public IP address on the Memorystore instance
Cloud CDN in front of the service
questions.explanation: Cloud Run services can send traffic into a VPC network with Direct VPC egress (or a Serverless VPC Access connector) and so reach private IPs such as a Memorystore instance. Memorystore does not offer a public endpoint, and a CDN or external load balancer handles inbound traffic, not outbound.

questions.stem: A finance director asks how moving from owned hardware to Google Cloud changes the company's spending. Which answer is most accurate?
options: All spending ends
Operating spending turns into one large up-front capital purchase
Spending stays the same, because hardware costs are passed on
Capital spending shifts mostly to operating spending
questions.explanation: Buying servers is capital expenditure (CapEx); paying for cloud resources as they are used is operating expenditure (OpEx). That shift lets spending follow demand but needs cost controls such as budgets, labels and rightsizing.

questions.stem: An application calling a Google Cloud API sometimes receives errors that mean the service is busy or the rate is exceeded. How should the client handle them?
options: Retry at once in a tight loop until it works
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter
Create a new project for every retry
Give up on the first error and report it
questions.explanation: For retryable errors such as rate limiting and temporary unavailability, Google recommends retrying with exponential backoff plus random jitter, so clients spread out and do not overload the service. Tight loops make congestion worse.

questions.stem: The security team wants to stop anyone in the organization creating service account keys, now and in future projects. What should it do?
options: Remove the IAM service from the list of enabled APIs everywhere
An email asking developers not to
An organization policy that disables key creation
Delete any keys it finds in a weekly manual review of projects
questions.explanation: Organization policy constraints, such as the one that disables service account key creation, apply to every project under the node where they are set, including new ones. Emails and manual reviews are not preventive controls, and IAM cannot be switched off.

questions.stem: A containerized job runs every night for about 40 minutes, processes a batch of files and then exits. It serves no web requests. Which option runs it with the least to manage?
options: A Cloud Run service with minimum instances
A GKE Standard cluster kept running all day
Cloud Run jobs on a schedule
A Compute Engine VM that is never stopped
questions.explanation: Cloud Run jobs run containers to completion and stop, and Cloud Scheduler can trigger them on a timetable, so nothing runs or bills between batches. Cloud Run services are for handling requests, and an always-on cluster or VM pays for idle hours.

questions.stem: A team wants metrics and logs from Compute Engine VMs, including memory and disk use, in Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging. What should it install?
options: The Ops Agent
A Cloud Router per VM
Cloud Code on each VM
The Spanner emulator
questions.explanation: The Ops Agent collects system metrics such as memory and disk use, which the hypervisor cannot see, plus application logs, and sends them to Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging. Cloud Code is an IDE extension and the emulator is for local testing.

questions.stem: A company is moving to GKE, but its operations team has never run Kubernetes. What should the architect recommend in the plan?
options: Assess skills early and train the team before production
Avoid documentation so the team learns by fixing outages
Hire a contractor to run the cluster and keep the team uninvolved
Delay any training until after the cluster is in production use
questions.explanation: Skills readiness is part of the migration plan: assess where the gaps are, train or pair people early and build up with lower-risk workloads. Leaving the team out or learning during outages raises operational risk.

questions.stem: A team writing Python code to read and write Cloud Storage objects asks which approach Google recommends. What should the architect say?
options: Cloud Client Libraries with Application Default Credentials
Call gsutil from Python with a shell command for every object
Build raw HTTP requests and paste an access token into the code
Personal API keys in the code
questions.explanation: The Cloud Client Libraries are idiomatic for each language and handle authentication through Application Default Credentials, retries and paging. Hard-coded tokens or keys are a security risk, and shelling out to a CLI is fragile.

questions.stem: Administrators need SSH access to VMs that have no external IP addresses, controlled by their identity rather than by network location. What should be used?
options: Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding
External IP addresses on each VM
A public bastion host open to the internet
A shared SSH key emailed to every admin
questions.explanation: IAP TCP forwarding tunnels SSH to VMs with only internal IPs, and access is granted by IAM role and can include context such as device posture. A public bastion or external IPs widen the attack surface, and shared keys remove accountability.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. Before any patient data is stored in Google Cloud, which step does the company need to take with Google?
options: Encrypt every record with a key stored in the application code
Request a dedicated support engineer to review each deployment
Ask Google to place the projects in a separate private data center
Sign a Business Associate Agreement and use only covered products
questions.explanation: Under HIPAA, a covered entity that stores protected health information with a cloud provider needs a Business Associate Agreement, and the PHI should be kept in the services covered by it. Google Cloud does not offer private data centers, and keys in application code are a security flaw, not a control.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. Which storage approach fits the imaging archive that is rarely read after the first year but kept for many years?
options: A Bigtable table with one row for every image file stored
Persistent Disk snapshots kept on a VM in each clinic's region
Cloud Storage with lifecycle rules to Archive
Memorystore with the images in memory
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage holds large unstructured objects such as images, and Object Lifecycle Management can move them to colder, cheaper classes such as Archive as they age. Bigtable is for small, high-throughput rows, and an in-memory cache or VM disks would cost far more for data that is rarely read.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. Which design fits the call-center summary feature?
options: A model saves summaries straight into patient records unchecked
A model trained only on public medical forums writes the notes
Staff write every summary by hand while the model stays unused
A Gemini model drafts summaries that staff review before saving
questions.explanation: The case says the AI drafts summaries for staff to review, which keeps a human in the loop for records about patients. Saving output unchecked removes that review, and a model trained on public forums is neither grounded nor appropriate for clinical notes.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. Which control meets the requirement that patient data must not leave a defined perimeter even if a credential is stolen?
options: A stronger staff password policy
A VPC firewall rule that denies all ingress traffic from the internet
A VPC Service Controls perimeter around those projects
Moving the patient data to a bucket in a different Google Cloud region
questions.explanation: VPC Service Controls creates a service perimeter around projects so that Google APIs such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery cannot move data to resources outside it, even when called with valid stolen credentials. Firewall rules control VM network traffic, not API data movement.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. How should the architect meet the requirement that the company holds its own encryption keys for patient data?
options: Base64-encoded patient records
Rely on Google's default encryption with keys that Google manages
Customer-managed encryption keys in Cloud KMS
Store a single key in the application's configuration file in Git
questions.explanation: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS let the company create, rotate, disable and audit the keys that protect its data in services such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery. Default encryption uses Google-managed keys, a key in Git is exposed, and Base64 is encoding, not encryption.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. How should the team meet the requirement that developers never see real patient data in test environments?
options: Copy production data to test and ask developers not to look
Give developers the same production access as clinicians
Use de-identified or synthetic data in test environments
Encrypt production data and share the key with developers
questions.explanation: Test environments should use data that has been de-identified, for example with Sensitive Data Protection, or that is synthetic, so real patient information never reaches them. Copying production data, even encrypted with a shared key, still exposes it.

questions.stem: Refer to the Pinecrest Clinics case study. The team wants to move the PostgreSQL booking database to a managed service with minimal downtime. Which tool should the architect recommend?
options: Storage Transfer Service copying the database's data files directly
Database Migration Service with continuous replication to Cloud SQL
A nightly pg_dump file copied to a Cloud Storage bucket by hand
Transfer Appliance shipped to the clinic data center with the tables
questions.explanation: Database Migration Service replicates PostgreSQL continuously into Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, so the cutover needs only a short pause while the last changes catch up. Dump files mean downtime and data loss between dumps, and file transfer tools cannot copy a running database safely.

questions.stem: Leadership asks how it will know a migration to Google Cloud was worth it. Which measure is the best primary KPI to agree before the project starts?
options: Cost and release frequency against a baseline
The count of Google Cloud products the teams have tried so far
The first month's cloud bill
The number of VMs moved to Google Cloud each week of the project
questions.explanation: Success measures should tie to business outcomes and be compared with a baseline measured before the change, such as cost per transaction and how often teams can ship. VM counts track activity, not value, and a single month's bill ignores the migration overlap.

questions.stem: A team runs a GKE cluster where some workloads are fault-tolerant batch jobs and others are customer-facing APIs. How should it place them to save money safely?
options: Batch jobs on Spot VM nodes, APIs on standard nodes
APIs on Spot VM nodes, batch jobs on standard nodes
Every workload on Spot VM nodes for the lowest price
Every workload on standard nodes with no commitments
questions.explanation: Spot VM node pools are much cheaper but nodes can be reclaimed at any time, which suits work that can retry. Customer-facing APIs belong on standard nodes. Node selectors, taints and tolerations keep each workload on the right pool.

questions.stem: A company wants an inventory of its 2,000 on-premises servers, their utilization and a cost estimate for running them on Google Cloud before it commits to a plan. Which tool should it start with?
options: Database Migration Service
Migration Center
Cloud Deploy
Storage Transfer Service
questions.explanation: Migration Center discovers and assesses existing servers, collects utilization data, and produces cost estimates and recommendations for the migration. Database Migration Service and Storage Transfer Service move databases and files once the plan exists, and Cloud Deploy releases applications.

questions.stem: A company wants to pull invoice numbers and totals from scanned supplier invoices, and to transcribe customer voicemails into text, without training its own models. Which two products fit? (Choose two.)
options: Cloud Translation
BigQuery ML linear regression
Speech-to-Text
Document AI with an invoice processor
A custom model trained from scratch on TPUs
questions.explanation: Document AI has pre-trained processors that extract fields such as totals and invoice numbers from documents, and Speech-to-Text transcribes audio. A custom model is unnecessary for common tasks that pre-trained APIs already handle, and Translation converts text between languages.

questions.stem: A team wants to find out how its service behaves when a dependency fails, before that happens for real. Which practice is designed for this?
options: Adding the dependency to a second billing account
Removing the dependency from all monitoring
Waiting for a real outage and studying the logs
Chaos engineering with controlled fault injection
questions.explanation: Chaos engineering deliberately injects failures, such as dropping a dependency or adding latency, in a controlled way and with a limited blast radius, to find weaknesses before real incidents do. Waiting for an outage learns the same lesson at a much higher price.

questions.stem: A large retailer's store managers resist a new cloud-based stock system that changes how they order goods. What is the best first step?
options: Ask head office to issue an order that managers use the new system
Run both systems forever
Involve the managers early and explain the benefits
Switch the old system off on a fixed date with no notice to stores
questions.explanation: Organizational change succeeds when affected people are involved early, understand why the change helps them and see their concerns addressed, followed by training and support. Forced cutovers and mandates without engagement build resistance.

questions.stem: A new contractor needs to run gcloud and edit a few configuration files today, on a locked-down laptop where nothing can be installed. What should they use?
options: An emailed copy of the files edited in a word processor
Cloud Shell with the Cloud Shell Editor in the browser
A local install of the Google Cloud CLI on the laptop
A new Compute Engine VM with an external IP for each user
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell is a browser-based terminal with the gcloud CLI and other tools preinstalled and already authenticated, and the Cloud Shell Editor provides an IDE in the same browser tab. Nothing needs to be installed on the laptop.

questions.stem: A company wants GKE to run only container images that were built by its own pipeline and passed vulnerability checks. What should the architect configure?
options: A firewall rule that blocks image downloads from the internet
Binary Authorization with attestations from the build pipeline
A larger node pool so scanning finishes faster on each node
Public read access on Artifact Registry so anyone can check images
questions.explanation: Binary Authorization enforces deploy-time policy so that only images with the required attestations, such as "built by our pipeline" and "passed scanning", can run on GKE or Cloud Run. Firewalls and node sizes do not check image provenance, and public registries weaken security.

questions.stem: A team's Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database must be recoverable to any minute in the last 7 days and must survive a regional disaster. Which two settings should the architect specify? (Choose two.)
options: Create a cross-region read replica to promote in a disaster
Enable point-in-time recovery on the instance
Export a daily SQL dump to a bucket in the same region
Turn on high availability with a standby in another zone
Increase the storage size so automatic backups are kept longer
questions.explanation: Point-in-time recovery replays the write-ahead logs so the database can be restored to a chosen minute. A cross-region read replica can be promoted if the primary region is lost. The zonal standby of an HA instance protects against a zone failure only, and a same-region dump does not survive a regional disaster.

questions.stem: An operations team must patch the operating systems of 800 Compute Engine VMs on a schedule and report which ones are still missing patches. Which two choices help? (Choose two.)
options: VM Manager patch deployments with maintenance windows
Recreating every VM from a public image each week
Logging in to each VM over SSH once a month
Turning off automatic restart on every VM
OS patch compliance reports from VM Manager
questions.explanation: VM Manager (OS Config) can schedule patch jobs across fleets of VMs during maintenance windows and reports patch compliance. Manual SSH does not scale, rebuilding every VM weekly is disruptive without a tested image pipeline, and automatic restart has nothing to do with patching.

questions.stem: A retailer needs a private, high-bandwidth link from its data center to Google Cloud with dynamic routing, and an encrypted backup path if that link fails. Which two components should the architect choose? (Choose two.)
options: Dedicated Interconnect with Cloud Router
HA VPN as the backup path
VPC Network Peering to the data center
Cloud NAT on the data center side
Private Google Access on every subnet
questions.explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides private, high-capacity circuits, and Cloud Router exchanges routes with BGP. HA VPN gives an encrypted IPsec path over the internet that can take over if the circuits fail. Cloud NAT handles outbound internet traffic, and VPC peering connects VPC networks, not data centers.

questions.stem: Which two practices are part of the operational excellence pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
options: Release all changes at once each quarter to reduce how often teams deploy
Give every engineer the Owner role so work is never blocked
Avoid monitoring production so that costs stay as low as possible
Manage incidents and problems, and learn from each one
Automate and manage change through repeatable processes
questions.explanation: The operational excellence pillar covers operational readiness, managing incidents and problems, managing and optimizing resources, automating and managing change, and continuous improvement. Broad access, no monitoring and big quarterly releases work against it.

questions.stem: A team wants confidence that infrastructure changes defined in Terraform will not break production. Which two practices help? (Choose two.)
options: Apply changes to a staging environment built from the same code first
Apply changes directly in production to save time on reviews
Keep a separate, hand-written copy of the code for each environment
Edit production resources in the console and update the code later
Review terraform plan output in a pull request before applying
questions.explanation: Reviewing the plan shows exactly what will change, and applying the same code to a production-like staging environment first catches problems early. Direct production changes and console drift mean the code no longer describes what runs.

questions.stem: Before a product launch, the team wants to know whether the new Cloud Run service and its database will hold the expected peak. Which two steps belong in the test plan? (Choose two.)
options: Test with a single request and multiply the result by the peak
Run the load test against production with no warning to anyone
Load test a production-like environment at and above expected peak
Skip the database in the test because it is a managed service
Watch latency, errors and database saturation during the test
questions.explanation: A useful load test drives realistic traffic at and beyond the expected peak against a production-like environment and watches the service's latency and errors and the database's limits. One request says nothing about concurrency, and managed databases still have capacity limits.

questions.stem: Auditors require a record of every read of sensitive Cloud Storage objects, kept for years in a place that administrators cannot alter. Which two steps meet this? (Choose two.)
options: Route the logs with a sink to a locked retention bucket
Keep the logs only in the default bucket with default retention
Rely on Admin Activity logs, which record every object read
Enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage
Turn off Cloud Logging to reduce the number of log entries
questions.explanation: Admin Activity logs record configuration changes and are always on, but reads of data are Data Access logs, which must be enabled for most services. A sink to a log bucket or storage bucket with a locked retention policy keeps them for years and protects them from changes.

questions.stem: A company wants developers to deploy to production but never manage IAM, and security admins to manage IAM but never deploy code. What principle is this, and how is it applied?
options: Defense in depth, with the same broad role granted to everyone
Separation of duties, with roles split across groups
Zero trust, with all access granted through one shared account
Least privilege, with Owner for both
questions.explanation: Separation of duties splits sensitive tasks so no single person can complete a risky change alone. In Google Cloud it is applied by granting distinct predefined or custom roles to different groups, often in different projects or folders. Broad or shared roles defeat it.

questions.stem: A team wants every change that passes tests to be released to production in stages, with an approval before the production step. Which product manages the promotion between environments?
options: Cloud Shell
Migration Center
Cloud Scheduler
Cloud Deploy
questions.explanation: Cloud Deploy defines delivery pipelines that promote releases through targets such as test, staging and production, with approvals and rollbacks, for GKE and Cloud Run. Cloud Build usually builds and tests the artifacts that Cloud Deploy releases.

questions.stem: Which command-line tool is used to run queries and manage datasets in BigQuery?
options: terraform
ssh
bq
kubectl
questions.explanation: The bq tool, part of the Google Cloud CLI, runs queries, loads data and manages BigQuery datasets and tables. kubectl manages Kubernetes clusters, and Terraform provisions infrastructure from code.

questions.stem: A global web application serves users on every continent and needs one anycast IP, TLS termination and URL-based routing to back ends in several regions. Which load balancer fits?
options: Regional internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
Regional external passthrough Network Load Balancer
Global external Application Load Balancer
questions.explanation: The global external Application Load Balancer gives a single anycast IP, terminates TLS at Google's edge and routes by host and path to back ends in many regions. Passthrough network load balancers work at the TCP and UDP level in one region, and internal load balancers serve private traffic.

questions.stem: A service has used its whole error budget for the quarter halfway through. Under common SRE practice, what should the team do?
options: Stop measuring the SLI
Slow releases and focus on reliability
Release features faster to make up for lost time
Raise the SLO target so the budget looks larger
questions.explanation: An error budget is the unreliability the SLO allows. When it is spent, teams usually slow or freeze risky releases and put effort into reliability until the service is back within its objective. Changing the target or the measurement hides the problem.

questions.stem: During discovery, a stakeholder says the new booking system "must be secure." What should the architect do with this statement?
options: Record it as written for each team
Agree specific, testable requirements with them
Treat it as a functional requirement for the login page only
Drop it, since Google Cloud is secure by default in every case
questions.explanation: Vague requirements cannot be designed or tested. Working with the stakeholder to turn "secure" into specifics, such as data classification, encryption, access rules and audit needs, gives teams a target. Google secures the infrastructure, but customers are responsible for how they configure their own resources.

questions.stem: Private VMs with no external IP must download operating system updates from the internet, and no inbound connections from the internet should be possible. What should be configured?
options: An external IP address on every VM
An internal Application Load Balancer
A VPC peering connection to the internet
Cloud NAT on a regional Cloud Router
questions.explanation: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for VMs without external IPs and does not accept unsolicited inbound connections. Giving each VM an external IP exposes it, peering does not connect to the internet, and an internal load balancer distributes private traffic.

questions.stem: The security team must block a list of known malicious IP ranges for every VPC network in the organization, and project owners must not be able to override it. What should it use?
options: An IAM deny policy on the Compute Engine service
A Cloud NAT rule that drops outbound traffic
A hierarchical firewall policy on the organization
A VPC firewall rule added by hand in each project
questions.explanation: Hierarchical firewall policies are set on the organization or folders and are evaluated before VPC firewall rules, so central rules apply everywhere and cannot be loosened by project owners. Per-project rules can be changed locally, and IAM policies do not filter network traffic.

questions.stem: A payments service must recover within minutes after a regional outage, with almost no data loss. Which DR design fits?
options: Rebuild the service from scratch by hand in a new region when needed
Two regions with replicated data and automated failover
Nightly backups in the same region
Keep a written runbook only, with no infrastructure in a second region
questions.explanation: A very short RTO and near-zero RPO call for a hot or active-active design: capacity already running in a second region and data replicated so a regional failure loses little or nothing, for example with a multi-region Spanner configuration. Same-region backups and manual rebuilds are far too slow.

questions.stem: Developers want to write, run and debug Kubernetes and Cloud Run applications from inside their usual VS Code or JetBrains IDE. Which tool is designed for this?
options: Cloud Code
Cloud NAT
Cloud Armor
Cloud Router
questions.explanation: Cloud Code is a set of IDE extensions for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs that help develop, deploy and debug applications on GKE and Cloud Run, with Google Cloud APIs and Gemini Code Assist integration. The other products are networking and security services.

questions.stem: A SaaS provider on Google Cloud wants customers in their own VPC networks to reach its API through a private IP in each customer's network, without VPC peering. What should it use?
options: VPC Network Peering with each customer
A public IP protected by Cloud Armor
Private Service Connect
Cloud NAT
questions.explanation: Private Service Connect lets a producer publish a service behind an internal load balancer, and consumers reach it through an endpoint with an internal IP in their own VPC. It avoids peering, overlapping address problems and exposing the service to the internet.

questions.stem: A research lab must train a very large model for several weeks and wants the best price for performance on Google's own accelerators, using frameworks such as JAX. Which hardware fits best?
options: Cloud TPUs
Local SSD attached to standard VMs
Shared-core VMs
Memory-optimized VMs with no accelerator
questions.explanation: Cloud TPUs are Google's accelerators designed for large-scale ML training and serving, and they are part of the AI Hypercomputer along with GPUs, networking and storage. CPU-only VMs and local disks do not provide the accelerator compute that large training runs need.

questions.stem: A company has 300 projects and wants every project's audit and application logs kept in one place that the security team can query with SQL. What should the architect configure?
options: Logs exported by hand from each project to spreadsheets every week
A separate log bucket in each project that the security team checks one by one
Log retention turned off in every project to reduce the volume
An aggregated organization sink to a central log bucket
questions.explanation: An aggregated sink created at the organization or a folder routes logs from every project below it to one destination, such as a central log bucket. With Log Analytics enabled on that bucket, the security team can query the logs with SQL. Per-project checks and manual exports do not scale.

questions.stem: A ticketing site sees almost no traffic most of the year and huge bursts when sales open. Which design best matches cost to demand?
options: Stateless services on Cloud Run that scale on demand
A single GKE node pool with autoscaling turned off
A fixed pool of large VMs sized for the busiest sale ever
One VM per customer created by hand before each sale
questions.explanation: Stateless containers on Cloud Run scale with incoming requests and can scale to zero between sales, so the company pays for what it uses. A fixed pool sized for peak wastes money most of the year, and manual or non-autoscaling designs cannot follow a sudden burst.

questions.stem: Logs in a bucket are read often for 30 days, rarely for a year, and must then be deleted. What is the simplest way to manage cost?
options: A daily script that copies logs to a new bucket in a cheaper class
Object Versioning turned on so old copies are kept in the bucket
Persistent Disk snapshots of the VM where the logs were first written
Lifecycle rules that change the class with age and delete at one year
questions.explanation: Object Lifecycle Management changes an object's storage class or deletes it based on conditions such as age, with no code to run. Copy scripts add work and failure points, snapshots are for disks, and versioning keeps more copies rather than fewer.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Which business requirement most directly argues for autoscaling services rather than a fixed fleet?
options: The tutor must refuse off-topic or unsafe requests
Traffic grows tenfold before exams
Parental consent rules must be met in every country
Teams want independent releases
questions.explanation: A tenfold seasonal peak, with the stated need for cost to fall back afterward, is the case for capacity that scales out and back in. Independent releases point to CI/CD and service boundaries, and the consent and tutor rules are compliance and AI safety requirements.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Which change most directly lowers video latency for learners in Europe and Asia?
options: Add more vCPUs to the Compute Engine VMs in the US region
Move the database to a larger Cloud SQL machine type in the US
Turn on Object Versioning on the bucket that holds the videos
Serve the videos through Cloud CDN on a global load balancer
questions.explanation: Cloud CDN caches content at Google's edge locations close to users, so videos stored in one region are served from nearby caches worldwide. A bigger database or more web server CPU does not shorten the distance to distant learners, and versioning protects objects rather than speeding them up.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Before the exam season, the company is worried about bots and layer 7 attacks overwhelming its web front end. What should the architect configure?
options: VPC firewall rules that allow only the company's office IP range
Private Google Access on the subnet that holds the web servers
A bigger machine type for the Cloud SQL database primary
Cloud Armor security policies on the external load balancer
questions.explanation: Cloud Armor attaches to external Application Load Balancers and filters traffic at Google's edge with rate limiting, bot management, preconfigured WAF rules and DDoS protection. Allowing only office IPs would block learners, and database size or Private Google Access does nothing against attack traffic.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Which control most directly helps the tutor meet its requirement to refuse unsafe requests?
options: Run the tutor on Spot VMs to lower its cost
Raise the model's temperature for tutor answers
Screen prompts and responses with Model Armor
Store tutor logs in a Nearline storage bucket
questions.explanation: Model Armor screens prompts and model responses for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, harmful content and sensitive data, so unsafe or manipulated requests can be blocked. Temperature changes how varied answers are, and the storage class or VM type has no effect on safety.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Which approach best meets the children's data requirement across the countries it serves?
options: Leave privacy rules to each school, since schools already sign contracts
Store children's data in any region that has the lowest price for storage
Treat every learner as an adult so a single privacy policy covers them all
Map each country's rules and build consent and data limits into the design
questions.explanation: Children's privacy laws differ by country, so the architect must identify which apply and design for them: parental consent where required, collecting only the data needed, and controls on storage location and retention. Treating children as adults or passing the duty to schools does not meet the business requirement.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. Which change best supports teams releasing features independently and daily?
options: Ask every team to wait for the operations team to deploy their code
Keep one monthly release but add a second approver to sign it off
Freeze all changes during exam weeks and release twice a year
Split the monolith into services with their own automated pipelines
questions.explanation: Independent, frequent releases need independently deployable services, each with its own CI/CD pipeline, tests and rollback. Extra sign-off or centralized deployment keeps the monthly bottleneck that causes the rollbacks the case describes.

questions.stem: Refer to the Brightwave Learning case study. How should the team gain confidence before the next exam season that the platform will hold the tenfold peak?
options: Load test beyond the expected peak in a production-like setup
Assume autoscaling will cope because it is a managed feature
Wait for the exam season and add capacity if pages are slow
Run a short test with one user and multiply the result by ten
questions.explanation: Load testing beyond the expected peak shows whether autoscaling, quotas, the database and caches hold up, and leaves time to fix limits before exam weeks. Autoscaling still depends on quotas and on parts that do not scale automatically, such as the database.

questions.stem: An engineer sometimes needs to run admin scripts as a privileged service account. What is the most secure way to allow this?
options: Grant the Token Creator role so the engineer impersonates it
Share the service account's key file in the team chat when needed
Give the engineer's user account the same broad roles permanently
Download a key for the service account onto the engineer's laptop
questions.explanation: Impersonation lets an authorized user obtain short-lived credentials for a service account without any key file, and every use is logged. Downloaded or shared keys are long-lived secrets, and permanent broad roles break least privilege.

questions.stem: Why should application releases be built once as an artifact and the same artifact promoted through test, staging and production?
options: So developers can skip writing unit tests
So production runs exactly what was tested
So each environment can use a different version
So builds take place only in production
questions.explanation: Building once and promoting the same immutable artifact, such as a container image in Artifact Registry, ensures that what reaches production is exactly what passed testing. Rebuilding per environment can introduce differences.

questions.stem: A platform team wants Google to run Terraform for it, with state and execution managed in Google Cloud and every deployment recorded. Which service fits?
options: Artifact Analysis scans
Migration Center
Cloud Shell Editor
Infrastructure Manager
questions.explanation: Infrastructure Manager runs Terraform configurations as a managed Google Cloud service, storing state and keeping a record of each deployment and revision. Cloud Shell Editor is a browser IDE, and Artifact Analysis scans images for vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: A legacy application on Compute Engine VMs expects a shared POSIX file system that several VMs mount at once over NFS. Which product meets this without code changes?
options: Bigtable
Local SSD on each VM
Filestore
Cloud Storage with signed URLs
questions.explanation: Filestore is a managed NFS file server that many VMs and GKE pods can mount at the same time. Cloud Storage is object storage reached through an API, and Local SSD is temporary storage attached to one VM only.

questions.stem: A release of a Cloud Run service is causing errors. What is the fastest safe way to restore service?
options: Raise the memory limit and hope the errors stop
Delete the service and redeploy it from scratch
Shift all traffic back to the previous revision
Wait for the next scheduled release window
questions.explanation: Cloud Run keeps earlier revisions, so traffic can be moved back to the last good revision in seconds while the team investigates. Deleting and redeploying takes longer, and waiting or guessing leaves users affected.

questions.stem: A company wants employees to reach internal web apps without a VPN, but only from managed devices that meet its security policy. Which solution fits?
options: Private Google Access on the subnets of the apps
Chrome Enterprise Premium with Identity-Aware Proxy
Cloud NAT in front of each internal application
Public IP addresses for the apps with a shared password
questions.explanation: Chrome Enterprise Premium (formerly BeyondCorp Enterprise) and IAP give zero trust access: each request is checked against user identity and device context such as management status. A shared password ignores context, and Cloud NAT and Private Google Access are about outbound traffic.

questions.stem: A trading dashboard reads the same reference data thousands of times a second from Cloud SQL, and read latency is too high. What is the most direct improvement?
options: Cache the reference data in Memorystore
Turn on point-in-time recovery for the Cloud SQL instance
Move the database to Archive storage
Add more vCPUs to the web servers that call the database
questions.explanation: Data that is read far more often than it changes is a good fit for an in-memory cache such as Memorystore, which serves reads in sub-millisecond time and takes load off the database. Extra web server CPU does not shorten database reads, and recovery settings do not affect read speed.

questions.stem: A GKE workload's CPU use swings widely during the day. Which combination lets the pods and the cluster both grow and shrink with demand?
options: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and cluster autoscaler
A fixed replica count with a fixed number of nodes
A cron job that deletes pods every evening at six
Vertical scaling of the control plane by Google only
questions.explanation: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler adds or removes pod replicas from metrics such as CPU, and the cluster autoscaler adds nodes when pods cannot be scheduled and removes underused nodes. Fixed counts cannot follow demand, and deleting pods on a schedule ignores the actual load.

questions.stem: Teams keep building their own slightly different VPC and project setups, and many fail security review. What should the platform team provide?
options: A single shared project in which every team creates its resources
Approved infrastructure modules that teams reuse
A monthly setup review meeting
A rule that every team must design its own network from the start
questions.explanation: A curated catalog of approved templates, such as reviewed Terraform modules for projects and networks, lets teams provision quickly while staying within security and cost guardrails. Building from scratch or sharing one project leads to drift and weak isolation.

questions.stem: A small team needs to put authentication and basic rate limiting in front of a few serverless APIs on Cloud Run, without a full API program. Which product is the lighter fit?
options: Cloud Interconnect
API Gateway
Apigee with monetization
Bigtable
questions.explanation: API Gateway is a managed gateway for serverless back ends such as Cloud Run and Cloud Run functions, offering authentication and basic traffic control. Apigee adds full API lifecycle features such as monetization and developer portals, which a small internal need may not justify.

questions.stem: A regulator requires the bank's encryption keys to be protected by hardware security modules validated to FIPS 140-2 Level 3. What should the architect choose?
options: Cloud HSM keys in Cloud KMS
Software keys in a Secret Manager secret
Default keys
Keys kept in a VM's local file system
questions.explanation: Cloud HSM lets customers create and use keys protected by FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules, managed through the Cloud KMS API. Default encryption and software keys do not meet a hardware requirement, and keys in a VM's file system are poorly protected.

questions.stem: A team wants to run containerized microservices on Kubernetes but does not want to manage nodes, node pools or their sizing. Which option fits?
options: GKE Standard with manual node pools
Compute Engine VMs with Docker installed
GKE Autopilot
VMware Engine
questions.explanation: In GKE Autopilot, Google manages the nodes and their scaling, and the team pays for the resources its pods request. GKE Standard gives control over nodes but leaves their management to the team, and VMs with Docker have no Kubernetes control plane at all.

questions.stem: A team supports a critical application and wants faster incident response at 3 a.m. What should it prepare in advance?
options: A plan to rebuild the system from scratch each time
A rule that only the original developer can respond
Runbooks for common failures linked from the alerts
A list of personal phone numbers kept by one manager
questions.explanation: Runbooks give on-call engineers tested steps for known failure modes, and linking them from alerts saves time when it matters. Relying on one person or rebuilding each time makes incidents longer.

questions.stem: Two business units disagree on whether a shared data platform should favor low cost or low latency. As the architect, what should you do?
options: Make the trade-off explicit with data and help the sponsors decide
Delay the project until the two units reach agreement on their own
Choose the option your own team prefers and announce the result
Build two separate platforms so that neither unit has to compromise
questions.explanation: An architect facilitates decisions by laying out each option's cost, latency and risk against the business goals and bringing the sponsors to an agreed choice. Deciding alone ignores stakeholders, and duplicate platforms or indefinite delay waste money.

questions.stem: An operations engineer wants an AI explanation of why a Cloud Run service is returning errors, using the logs and metrics already in the project. Which tool helps most directly?
options: Gemini Cloud Assist
Cloud Deploy
Cloud Shell Editor
Storage Transfer Service
questions.explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist can investigate issues by analyzing logs, metrics and configuration in the project and suggesting likely causes and fixes. The other tools edit code, move data or release software.

questions.stem: A customer's auditor asks for evidence that Google Cloud's controls were assessed under SOC 2. Where should the architect point them?
options: The VPC flow logs of the production network
The Cloud Shell history of the admin team
Google Cloud's Compliance Reports Manager
The project's billing export in BigQuery
questions.explanation: Google publishes third-party audit reports such as SOC 2 through the Compliance Reports Manager. Under the shared responsibility model, the customer still has to show its own controls, but Google's infrastructure attestation comes from those reports, not from project logs.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. A fixed pool of VMs for settlement and the warehouse feeds will run around the clock, unchanged, for years. Which purchasing option should the architect recommend for that baseline?
options: A committed use discount
Spot VMs for every job
On-demand VMs with no discount
Sole-tenant nodes with no commitment
questions.explanation: Committed use discounts lower the price of compute that runs predictably for one or three years, which suits a pool that runs around the clock. Spot VMs can be stopped at any time, which is risky for settlement runs that must finish, and plain on-demand pricing costs more for the same steady use. A commitment would not suit VMs that run only a few hours a day.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. Which approach moves the VMware estate within a year without rewriting vendor applications?
options: Migrate the VMs to Google Cloud VMware Engine
Refactor every application into Cloud Run services
Rebuild each server by hand on Compute Engine
Containerize the vendor software and run it on GKE
questions.explanation: Google Cloud VMware Engine runs native VMware vSphere in Google Cloud, so VMs can move with the same tools and the vendor's VMware-only support stays valid. Refactoring, rebuilding or containerizing would take longer and could break vendor support.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. Relationship managers want to ask questions across approved research notes and client files and get cited answers, without the bank building its own application. Which option fits best?
options: Gemini Enterprise with NotebookLM over the approved sources
BigQuery ML forecasting models built on the client files
A new custom model trained from scratch on the bank's TPUs
Cloud Vision API run over the research notes and client files
questions.explanation: Gemini Enterprise brings AI agents and NotebookLM to employees, and NotebookLM answers questions grounded in the sources a user provides, with citations. Training a model from scratch is far more work, the Vision API analyzes images, and forecasting models predict numbers rather than drafting briefings.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. How can the bank prove to auditors that no single administrator can both change and approve production access?
options: Split request and approval roles across groups, with audit logs
Give one trusted administrator the Owner role and ask them to keep a written log
Grant every administrator the same broad role so that anyone can cover absences
Firewall rules that block unapproved changes
questions.explanation: Separation of duties is shown by granting the right to request access and the right to approve it to different groups, so no one person holds both, with every grant and approval captured in Cloud Audit Logs. A single trusted Owner or identical broad roles defeat the control.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. How should the architect keep card data in a clearly scoped environment in Google Cloud?
options: Dedicated projects in their own folder and perimeter
Labels marking card resources, left in shared projects
The same project as the data warehouse, for easy joins
Copies of card data in every region for low latency
questions.explanation: A dedicated folder and projects for the cardholder data environment, with their own network, IAM and a VPC Service Controls perimeter, make the PCI DSS scope clear and enforceable. Sharing projects or relying on labels mixes card data with out-of-scope systems.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. Which approach to infrastructure change meets the requirement that every change is reviewed and reproducible?
options: Give one engineer production access and trust that person to be careful
Define infrastructure as code and apply it only through reviewed pipelines
Let each team change resources in the console and keep a weekly notes file
Allow emergency console changes and describe them later in an email
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code in version control, applied only by a pipeline after peer review, makes every change reviewable, auditable and repeatable. Console changes, notes and trusted individuals leave no reliable record and cannot be reproduced.

questions.stem: Refer to the Harborline Bank case study. Security wants scripts that call Google Cloud APIs to run as a service account, with no key files stored on admin machines. How should admins run them?
options: Use gcloud with service account impersonation from their own sign-in
Download one key for the service account and copy it to every laptop
Run the scripts as a personal account that has the basic Owner role
Paste the service account's private key into each script as a string
questions.explanation: The gcloud CLI and client libraries can impersonate a service account using the admin's own authenticated identity, given the Token Creator role, so short-lived tokens are used and each call is audited under the admin's name. Key files and embedded keys are long-lived secrets.

questions.stem: A review board wants a common checklist to judge new designs on reliability, security, cost and operations. Which Google resource is built for this?
options: The Google Cloud status dashboard
The Google Cloud pricing calculator
The Cloud Shell tutorials
The Well-Architected Framework
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Framework organizes best practices into pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance optimization, cost optimization and sustainability. The pricing calculator estimates cost only, and the status dashboard reports incidents.

questions.stem: A team must create identical VMs that self-heal when a health check fails and can be updated with a rolling replacement. What should it provision?
options: A managed instance group and template
VMs made in the console
A sole-tenant node group with no template
An unmanaged instance group of hand-built VMs
questions.explanation: A managed instance group creates identical VMs from an instance template, recreates VMs that fail health checks (autohealing) and supports rolling updates to a new template. Unmanaged groups and hand-built VMs have none of these features.

questions.stem: A company wants to move 500 VMs to Compute Engine quickly with minimal change, testing each wave in Google Cloud before cutover. Which service is built for this?
options: Cloud Build
Transfer Appliance shipments
Migrate to Virtual Machines
Database Migration Service
questions.explanation: Migrate to Virtual Machines replicates VMs from VMware, other clouds or physical servers to Compute Engine and supports test clones before cutover, which suits a wave-based rehost. Database Migration Service moves databases, Transfer Appliance moves bulk data offline, and Cloud Build builds code.

questions.stem: An ML team needs GPUs for short training experiments that can be interrupted, and also a guaranteed block of GPUs for a planned two-week training run next month. Which two options match these needs? (Choose two.)
options: On-demand CPUs only, since GPUs cannot be scheduled
Dynamic Workload Scheduler to reserve capacity for the planned run
A committed use discount for the short experiments
Spot VMs for the interruptible experiments
Shared-core VMs for the two-week training run
questions.explanation: Spot capacity is the cheapest way to run work that can be stopped and restarted. Dynamic Workload Scheduler, part of the AI Hypercomputer, obtains accelerator capacity for a planned window or as soon as it is available. Commitments suit steady long-term use, not short tests.

questions.stem: A company wants to run a penetration test against its own applications on Google Cloud. What does it need to do?
options: Disable all logging during the test so the results are not recorded anywhere
Follow the acceptable use policy; no notice to Google is needed
Get written permission from Google for every IP address before testing starts
Test only Google's infrastructure
questions.explanation: Google Cloud customers may test their own deployments without notifying Google, as long as they follow the acceptable use policy and terms of service. Tests should be scoped to the customer's own resources, and logging should stay on to capture findings.

questions.stem: Monthly cloud spend is rising and nobody can say which team or product drives it. What should the architect put in place first?
options: Consistent labels plus billing export to BigQuery
A single project for the whole company to keep billing simple
Only the CEO creates resources
Deleting the largest resources each month without asking
questions.explanation: Labels on resources, combined with a detailed billing export to BigQuery, let finance and teams see cost by team, product and environment. That visibility comes before budgets, alerts and optimization; blanket deletion or central approval for everything blocks work.

questions.stem: Code that calls Spanner is hard to unit test, because each test run touches a shared database. What should the architect advise?
options: Write tests only after the code has been in production for a month
Run every unit test against the shared production Spanner instance
Let users report the bugs
