Test logic against fakes or the Spanner emulator
questions.explanation: Unit tests should be fast and isolated: separating the data access layer lets logic be tested with fakes, and the local Spanner emulator supports tests that need real queries without a shared database. Testing against production risks data and interference.

questions.stem: A model is served from an Agent Platform endpoint. Security requires that application calls to it never cross the public internet and stay within the company's VPC Service Controls perimeter. What should the architect use?
options: A Cloud CDN cache placed in front of the public endpoint
A private endpoint reached through Private Service Connect
A public endpoint protected only by an API key in the app
Cloud NAT so the app reaches the endpoint from a fixed IP
questions.explanation: Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) supports private endpoints reached through Private Service Connect, so traffic stays on internal addresses, and the service can sit inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter. API keys, NAT and a CDN still leave the endpoint public.

questions.stem: After a lift-and-shift, a retailer wants its Google Cloud estate to keep improving without another big project. Which two practices support this? (Choose two.)
options: Review Recommender insights for rightsizing and idle resources
Move every workload to the newest product as soon as it launches
Plan small modernization steps tied to measured business goals
Remove monitoring after cutover to cut logging costs
Freeze the architecture until the next data center refresh
questions.explanation: Cloud-first improvement is continuous: act on Recommender findings such as idle VMs and oversized machine types, and modernize in small steps that each have a business reason. Freezing the design or chasing every new product both ignore the business case, and removing monitoring hides problems.

questions.stem: A team runs stateful databases on Compute Engine persistent disks and wants protection from both accidental deletion and a regional outage. Which two measures should it take? (Choose two.)
options: Schedule snapshots with a multi-region storage location
Turn off deletion protection so disks can be replaced faster
Use regional persistent disks for synchronous zone replication
Rely on Local SSD, since it survives a VM being deleted
Keep the only backups on the same disk in a second folder
questions.explanation: Scheduled snapshots stored in a multi-region location can restore disks after deletion or in another region. Regional persistent disks replicate writes across two zones, so a zone failure does not lose data. Local SSD is temporary storage tied to one VM and lost when it is deleted, and same-disk copies protect nothing.

questions.stem: While planning migration waves, an architect finds that a reporting service makes thousands of chatty calls a minute to a database that will move later. Which two actions reduce the risk? (Choose two.)
options: Measure the latency the hybrid link would add before deciding
Rewrite both systems before any migration starts
Move the service first and accept the extra latency without testing
Ignore the dependency because Interconnect removes all latency
Move the service and the database in the same wave
questions.explanation: Tightly coupled, chatty dependencies are usually migrated together, and the latency a hybrid connection adds should be measured and tested before splitting them. No network link removes latency, and a full rewrite delays the migration far more than the dependency calls for.

questions.stem: A platform team wants defects to be caught before they reach users rather than after. Which two quality control measures help most? (Choose two.)
options: Reducing log retention so fewer errors appear in reports
Releasing straight to all users and fixing problems afterward
Removing code review so changes reach production more quickly
Automated tests and policy checks that gate each pipeline stage
Progressive rollouts that watch metrics and stop on regressions
questions.explanation: Gates in the pipeline, such as tests, security scans and policy checks, stop bad changes early, and canary or progressive rollouts limit the blast radius and halt automatically when metrics worsen. Skipping review or hiding errors lets defects reach users.

questions.stem: After launch, a product team wants to know whether its new platform is actually helping customers. Which two measures are most useful? (Choose two.)
options: Adoption and task completion rates from product analytics
Customer-facing SLO attainment such as availability and latency
The count of commits pushed to the repository each week
The size of the team's container images in Artifact Registry
The number of Google Cloud projects the team has created
questions.explanation: Customer success is judged by outcomes customers feel: whether they adopt and complete tasks, and whether the service meets its customer-facing SLOs. Project counts, commit counts and image sizes describe internal activity, not customer value.

questions.stem: A team is moving a web app to GKE and wants releases that can be rolled back quickly and that never send traffic to pods that are not ready. Which two settings help? (Choose two.)
options: Readiness probes on the containers
Images tagged latest and pulled on every start
A Deployment with a rolling update strategy and revision history
A single pod with no replicas or probes
Host networking on every pod in the cluster
questions.explanation: Readiness probes keep traffic away from pods until they can serve, and a Kubernetes Deployment rolls updates gradually and keeps revision history so it can be rolled back. Mutable latest tags make it unclear which version is running.

questions.stem: A retailer processes card payments on Google Cloud and wants to keep its PCI DSS scope as small as possible. Which two design choices help most? (Choose two.)
options: Tokenize card numbers so other systems never store the real numbers
Give every developer access to production card data for debugging
Log full card numbers to help with troubleshooting payment errors
Isolate the cardholder data environment in its own projects and network
Store card numbers in the same database as product reviews
questions.explanation: Isolating the cardholder data environment and replacing card numbers with tokens keep most systems out of PCI DSS scope. Mixing card data with other data, broad developer access and logging card numbers all spread the scope and break the standard's requirements.

questions.stem: Which question is most useful for finding a workload's recovery point objective?
options: Which programming language is the application written in?
How many VMs does the application run on today?
How many users sign in to the system on a typical day?
How much recent data could the business afford to lose?
questions.explanation: The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. The recovery time objective is how long the system may be down. User counts, languages and VM counts help sizing, not recovery targets.

questions.stem: Two VPC networks, A and B, are peered, and B is also peered with C. Can VMs in A reach VMs in C through B?
options: Yes, because peering routes are shared with every peer
No, because VPC Network Peering is not transitive
Yes, as long as all three networks are in one region
No, because peered networks cannot share any routes
questions.explanation: VPC Network Peering exchanges subnet routes only between the two peered networks; it does not pass them on to a third. A and C would need their own peering, or a hub design such as Network Connectivity Center. Peered networks do share their subnet routes with each other.

questions.stem: A small company needs to connect its office to a VPC network this week over the internet, encrypted, with automatic failover between two tunnels. What should it set up?
options: Dedicated Interconnect at a colocation site
Private Service Connect with an endpoint
HA VPN with two tunnels and Cloud Router
VPC Network Peering to the office router
questions.explanation: HA VPN creates encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet, and with Cloud Router and BGP the traffic fails over between tunnels automatically. Dedicated Interconnect needs physical circuits at a colocation facility, which take longer to set up, and peering connects VPC networks only.

questions.stem: A retailer wants to label product photos with general objects such as shoes, bags and hats. What is the quickest approach?
options: Cloud Vision API label detection
Pixel color rules
Build a forecasting model in BigQuery ML
Train a custom image model on new TPUs
questions.explanation: For common, general-purpose labels, a pre-trained API such as Cloud Vision works immediately with no training data. Custom training is worth it when the labels are specific to the business, such as the company's own defect types.

questions.stem: Contractors should be able to start and stop VMs only until their contract ends on a set date. What feature lets the grant expire on its own?
options: A label on each VM showing the contract date
A Cloud Scheduler job that emails the contractors
A dated firewall rule
An IAM condition based on the request time
questions.explanation: IAM conditions can limit a role binding by attributes such as the request time or the resource name, so access stops automatically after a date. Firewall rule names and labels do not control IAM, and an email does not remove access.

questions.stem: A team wants to release a new version to 5% of users first, watch error rates, and then widen the rollout. What is this strategy called?
options: A big bang release
A rollback
A cold standby
A canary release
questions.explanation: A canary release sends a small share of traffic to the new version and widens it only if metrics stay healthy. A big bang release switches everyone at once, and cold standby is a disaster recovery pattern.

questions.stem: Which tool is the main command-line interface for creating and managing most Google Cloud resources, such as VMs and networks?
options: bq
kubectl
gcloud
pip
questions.explanation: The gcloud CLI manages most Google Cloud resources and is part of the Google Cloud CLI along with bq for BigQuery and gcloud storage (or the older gsutil) for Cloud Storage.

questions.stem: A team wants a chart and an alert for how often a specific error message appears in its application logs. What should it create?
options: A disk snapshot
A log-based metric
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
A new VPC network just for logs
questions.explanation: A log-based metric counts log entries that match a filter, such as a specific error message, and can be charted and alerted on in Cloud Monitoring. The other options do not turn logs into metrics.

questions.stem: A company's business continuity plan lists RTO 4 hours and RPO 1 hour for its order system. Which statement describes these targets correctly?
options: Backups must run every 4 hours and be kept for 1 hour each
Service must be back within 4 hours, losing at most 1 hour of data
Service must be back within 1 hour, losing at most 4 hours of data
The system may be down 4 hours a year and 1 hour a month
questions.explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) is how quickly service must return after a disruption, and the recovery point objective (RPO) is how much data, measured in time, may be lost. A 1-hour RPO means backups or replication at least every hour.

questions.stem: Every VM with the network tag "web" must accept HTTPS from the internet, and nothing else should change. What is the simplest rule?
options: A route sending TCP 443 traffic to the default gateway
An egress allow rule for TCP 443 on every VM in the VPC
An ingress allow rule for TCP 443 targeting the web tag
An ingress allow rule for all ports from any source
questions.explanation: VPC firewall rules can target VMs by network tag or service account. An ingress rule allowing TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 to the web tag opens HTTPS on those VMs only. Egress rules and routes do not admit inbound traffic, and allowing all ports is far too broad.

questions.stem: VMs in a VPC must resolve names in the company's on-premises DNS zone corp.example.internal over an existing Interconnect. What should the architect configure in Cloud DNS?
options: A firewall rule blocking DNS egress
A public zone for corp.example.internal published on the internet
A forwarding zone to the on-premises DNS servers
A peering zone pointing at a different project's VPC network
questions.explanation: A Cloud DNS forwarding zone sends queries for a chosen domain to target name servers, such as on-premises DNS reached over Interconnect or VPN. A public zone would expose internal names, and a peering zone resolves through another VPC's DNS configuration.

questions.stem: A manufacturer needs to spot its own specific defect types in factory images, which general image APIs do not recognize, and it has a few thousand labeled examples. Which approach fits?
options: Use the Cloud Vision API's general labels for every defect type
Ask a foundation model to guess defects with no examples at all
Wait for a better API
Train a custom model on Agent Platform
questions.explanation: When the categories are specific to the business and labeled data exists, training a custom model, for example with AutoML or custom training on Agent Platform, gives far better results than general labels. Waiting or guessing without examples does not meet the need.

questions.stem: No predefined role fits a support team that needs to view logs and restart one service, with nothing more. What should the architect create?
options: The basic Editor role on the project
A new organization for the support team
The basic Viewer role on the organization
A custom role with just those permissions
questions.explanation: Custom roles bundle exactly the permissions a job function needs when no predefined role fits, which follows least privilege. Basic roles are broad, and a separate organization does not grant the right access.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a blue/green deployment?
options: The new version is tested only after it is fully live in production
Each server is updated in turn while the others keep serving traffic
A small share of traffic tries it
Two full environments, with traffic switched between them
questions.explanation: Blue/green keeps two complete environments; the new version is deployed to the idle one and traffic switches over, which makes rollback a quick switch back. Updating servers in turn is a rolling update, and a small share of traffic is a canary.

questions.stem: An engineer needs to copy a large folder of files into a Cloud Storage bucket from the command line. Which command is designed for this?
options: gcloud storage cp, recursive
kubectl apply with the folder name
terraform import with the folder
bq load with the recursive flag
questions.explanation: gcloud storage cp (or the older gsutil cp) copies files and folders to and from Cloud Storage, with a recursive option for directories. bq load loads data into BigQuery tables, and kubectl and Terraform manage other resources.

questions.stem: A team wants to know from outside its network whether its public website is reachable from several locations around the world. What should it set up?
options: An uptime check
An internal load balancer
Bigtable
A Cloud Shell session
questions.explanation: Uptime checks in Cloud Monitoring probe a public URL or IP from several locations and can alert when the site stops responding. Internal load balancers serve private traffic, and the other options are not monitoring tools.

questions.stem: An inventory system must notify five other systems whenever stock changes, and new consumers will be added over time. Which integration pattern fits best?
options: Copy the inventory table to each consumer's database each night
Pub/Sub topic with a subscription per consumer
Let every consumer poll the inventory database every few seconds
Direct API calls from inventory to each one
questions.explanation: Publish and subscribe decouples the producer from its consumers: each consumer gets its own subscription and new ones can be added without changing the inventory system. Direct calls couple the systems, polling adds database load, and a nightly copy is far from real time.

questions.stem: A company runs workloads on Google Cloud and another public cloud and wants a private, high-bandwidth link between the two without building its own colocation setup. Which product is designed for this?
options: Partner Interconnect to the data center
Private Google Access
Cross-Cloud Interconnect
Cloud NAT on both sides
questions.explanation: Cross-Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated physical connections between Google Cloud and another cloud provider's network. Partner Interconnect links an on-premises network through a service provider, and Cloud NAT and Private Google Access handle outbound and Google API traffic.

questions.stem: Users in two cities in one country upload files to the same bucket and need low-latency access with data kept in that country. Which bucket location type fits best?
options: A multi-region bucket spanning several continents
A dual-region bucket in that country
A bucket in another country that has lower prices
A single-zone bucket
questions.explanation: A dual-region bucket stores data redundantly in two specific regions, which keeps it in the chosen country and serves both areas well. Multi-region locations span large areas such as a whole continent, and buckets are regional or wider, never single-zone.

questions.stem: Training data for a custom model lives in a large BigQuery table. A team plans to export it to CSV files before each training run. What should the architect advise?
options: Copy the table into Memorystore before every training run
Use the BigQuery table directly as the training data source
Email the CSV files to the data scientists for local training
Keep the CSV export, since Agent Platform cannot read BigQuery
questions.explanation: Agent Platform training can read data directly from BigQuery, which avoids export steps, stale copies and extra storage. Memorystore is a cache, and local training on emailed files loses governance and scale.

questions.stem: A company must be able to make its data in Google Cloud unreadable at once by withdrawing a key that it keeps entirely outside Google's infrastructure. Which option meets this?
options: Cloud External Key Manager with an outside key system
Default encryption at rest with keys that Google creates and manages
Keys typed in by developers
Customer-managed keys created in Cloud KMS inside the same project
questions.explanation: Cloud EKM lets supported services use keys held in an external key management system outside Google, so the company can deny access by withholding the key. Cloud KMS keys, including CMEK, live in Google's infrastructure.

questions.stem: Latency on a service rose after a release. What is the best first step in troubleshooting?
options: Compare metrics and traces from before and after the release
Add more features to the service to distract from the slowdown
Restart every VM in the project and wait to see what happens
Delete the logs to make room for new ones during the incident
questions.explanation: Root cause work starts with evidence: compare latency metrics, traces and logs around the change to see where time is now spent. If users are affected, rolling back while investigating is often right; random restarts destroy evidence.

questions.stem: A team discovers that someone changed a firewall rule in the console, so the live rule no longer matches the Terraform code. What is this called, and how is it usually found?
options: Configuration drift, found by running terraform plan
A canary release, found by checking the billing export
A cold start, found by watching Cloud Run latency
A rolling update, found by reading the audit log only
questions.explanation: When live resources differ from the code that should define them, that is drift. Running terraform plan compares the real state with the configuration and shows the differences, which the team then reconciles through code.

questions.stem: A team already uses Prometheus queries and dashboards and is moving its workloads to GKE. Which option lets it keep that approach without running its own Prometheus servers?
options: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus
Exporting all metrics to a spreadsheet every hour
Logs only, no metrics
A Prometheus server on one large VM with no backups
questions.explanation: Managed Service for Prometheus collects Prometheus metrics from GKE and stores them in a managed, scalable backend that PromQL and existing dashboards can query. A single self-run server is a reliability risk.

questions.stem: A company must move 400 TB of archived files from its data center to Cloud Storage, and its internet link is already busy during business hours. Which option should the architect consider first?
options: Emailing the files to Google support in batches
Transfer Appliance shipped to the data center
Mounting the bucket on one VM and dragging files in
Copying the files with gsutil over the existing link
questions.explanation: Transfer Appliance is a high-capacity storage device Google ships to the customer, who loads it and ships it back, which avoids saturating a busy network for weeks. Online tools such as Storage Transfer Service suit large transfers when there is enough spare bandwidth.

questions.stem: A GKE cluster must use IP addresses that are routable inside the VPC so pods can reach on-premises systems without NAT. Which cluster setting provides this?
options: A cluster with every node given an external IP
A cluster that uses host networking for each pod
A routes-based cluster
A VPC-native cluster using alias IP ranges
questions.explanation: VPC-native clusters assign pod and service addresses from secondary alias IP ranges of the subnet, so the VPC, peers and hybrid connections can route to pods directly. External node IPs expose nodes to the internet, and routes-based clusters are the older, less scalable mode.

questions.stem: An analytics team's dataset grows by several terabytes each month, and it pays for queries that scan whole tables even when only recent data is needed. What should be configured in BigQuery?
options: Turn off table expiration on every dataset
Copy the full table every day to a new dataset
Partition by date and cluster by common filters
Store the data in CSV files on a persistent disk
questions.explanation: Partitioning by date lets queries that filter on date scan only the relevant partitions, and clustering sorts data within partitions by frequently filtered columns. Both cut the bytes scanned and so the cost on on-demand pricing as data grows.

questions.stem: A team wants to use an open-weight model from Model Garden in its application, served on infrastructure it manages through Google Cloud. What is the usual next step?
options: Copy the model weights into a Cloud SQL table and query them with SQL
Share the model as a spreadsheet
Email the model provider to ask for a custom API key for each user
Deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint and call it
questions.explanation: Models from Model Garden can be deployed to an endpoint on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), which the application calls for predictions. A database table or a spreadsheet cannot serve a model.

questions.stem: Which Cloud Audit Logs type records changes to resource configuration, such as creating a VM or changing an IAM policy, and is always enabled?
options: VPC Flow Logs
Load balancer request logs
Admin Activity audit logs
Data Access audit logs
questions.explanation: Admin Activity logs record API calls that change configuration or metadata, are always written and cannot be turned off. Data Access logs record reads and data writes and are off by default for most services, and flow and request logs record network traffic.

questions.stem: A company has a DR plan but has never tried it. What should the architect recommend?
options: Keep the plan secret so attackers cannot learn the recovery steps
Assume the plan works because it was written by senior engineers
Test the plan once only, during the first real regional outage
Run regular DR drills that restore service in the recovery region
questions.explanation: A DR plan is only reliable if it is tested: scheduled drills prove that backups restore, infrastructure can be recreated and people know the steps, and they show whether RTO and RPO are met. Untested plans often fail when needed.

questions.stem: An Apigee policy can return an error once a partner exceeds its agreed number of calls per minute. What is this feature called?
options: A quota or spike arrest policy
A VPC Service Controls perimeter
A committed use discount
A lifecycle management rule
questions.explanation: Apigee policies such as Quota and SpikeArrest limit how many calls a client can make in a period, protecting back ends and enforcing partner agreements. The other options are storage, security and billing features.

questions.stem: Developers want new exceptions from their services grouped and counted, with a notification when a new kind of error first appears. Which service does this?
options: Cloud Deploy
Cloud Router
Error Reporting
Filestore snapshots
questions.explanation: Error Reporting groups application errors and exceptions from logs, counts them and can notify the team when a new error type appears. The other products route networks, release software and serve files.

questions.stem: When designing a new service, an architect is asked what observability requirements to set. Which answer is best?
options: Define its key signals, SLOs and alerts
Add monitoring after the first incident
Rely on users to report errors through the help desk
Log every request body in full at debug level forever
questions.explanation: Observability belongs in the design: decide which signals (latency, errors, traffic, saturation), service level objectives and alerts the service needs, and how logs and traces will be collected. Waiting for an incident, logging everything forever or relying on users all leave teams blind or overloaded.

questions.stem: A memory-hungry application needs 6 vCPUs and far more memory per vCPU than the predefined shapes offer, and the team wants to avoid paying for unused vCPUs. What should the architect choose?
options: Two smaller VMs behind a load balancer
The next larger predefined machine type
A custom machine type with extended memory
A shared-core machine type with swap enabled
questions.explanation: Custom machine types let teams pick the number of vCPUs and the amount of memory, and extended memory allows more memory per vCPU than the standard limit. Jumping to a larger predefined shape pays for vCPUs the app does not need.

questions.stem: A team's VMs need a GPU for video encoding only during business hours, and capacity must be available when the day starts. Which consideration matters most when choosing the zone?
options: Every zone offers every GPU type equally
The zone must offer that GPU type
GPUs work only on Spot VMs
GPUs require a sole-tenant node group
questions.explanation: GPU and accelerator types are available only in certain zones, so the zone must offer the required type and have capacity, which reservations can guarantee. GPUs can be used with standard or Spot VMs and do not need sole-tenant nodes.

questions.stem: A lightweight image-resizing model must run only when images are uploaded, scale to zero between uploads, and use a container the team already has. Which platform fits?
options: Cloud Run
Sole tenancy
VMware Engine
A GKE Standard cluster on fixed nodes
questions.explanation: Cloud Run runs containers on demand, scales with requests or events and scales to zero when idle, which suits light inference work. Fixed clusters, sole-tenant nodes and VMware private clouds keep paying for capacity between uploads.

questions.stem: A regulated customer wants to see when Google staff access its content during support work, and to approve that access first. Which pair of features does it need?
options: Cloud Trace and Cloud Profiler
Billing export and budget alerts
VPC Flow Logs and Cloud NAT logging
Access Transparency and Access Approval
questions.explanation: Access Transparency logs record actions Google personnel take on customer content, and Access Approval requires the customer's explicit approval before such access. The other pairs cover networking, cost and performance.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a business continuity plan and a disaster recovery plan?
options: Continuity restores IT; DR keeps the business running
They are the same plan with two names used by different teams
Continuity applies only to the cloud and DR only to data centers
Continuity keeps the business running; DR restores IT
questions.explanation: Business continuity planning covers how the whole organization keeps operating during a disruption, including people, processes and suppliers. Disaster recovery is the IT part: restoring systems and data within the agreed RTO and RPO.

questions.stem: A team must move a large MySQL database to Cloud SQL and keep the source live until a short cutover window. What is the main step before switching applications over?
options: Let replication catch up, stop writes, then promote
Delete the source database first so that no new writes can reach it
Export one dump at the start and accept every change made since then
Split writes across both for months
questions.explanation: With a continuous migration job, the target stays in sync while the source runs; at cutover, writes are stopped, the last changes replicate and the target is promoted. Deleting the source first or splitting writes between two databases risks data loss.

questions.stem: Before choosing between two machine families for a database, the team wants evidence of which performs better for its workload. What should it do?
options: Pick whichever family is listed first in the documentation
Ask a colleague which machine family they used on another project
Choose the family with the newest-sounding name in the console
Benchmark both with the real workload pattern and compare results
questions.explanation: Benchmarking each candidate with a representative workload gives evidence about throughput, latency and cost per transaction for this use case. Names, list order and other projects' choices say little about this workload.

questions.stem: A global game must keep players' inventory strongly consistent across continents. Why might an architect accept Spanner's higher cost over a single-region Cloud SQL database?
options: It is the only Google database that supports SQL
It removes the need to design keys, schemas or indexes
It stores data on players' own devices to cut latency
Strongly consistent writes across regions at scale
questions.explanation: Spanner provides externally consistent transactions across regions and scales horizontally, which a single-region relational instance cannot. Cloud SQL and AlloyDB also support SQL, and Spanner still needs careful schema and key design to avoid hotspots.

questions.stem: Analysts want to query Parquet files that land in Cloud Storage each hour using SQL in BigQuery, without loading them into native tables first. What should the architect set up?
options: A Memorystore cache in front of the bucket
A nightly export of the files to Cloud SQL
A Filestore share mounted by each analyst
BigLake or external tables over the bucket
questions.explanation: BigQuery can query files in Cloud Storage in place through external tables, and BigLake tables add fine-grained access control over them. Loading into Cloud SQL or caching the files does not give analysts SQL over the data where it lands.

questions.stem: A containerized web API must keep latency low for the first request after quiet periods. Which Cloud Run setting addresses cold starts?
options: Set a minimum number of instances
Turn off request-based billing
Set the maximum instances to one
Reduce the memory limit to the lowest
questions.explanation: Setting minimum instances keeps some container instances warm, so requests after a quiet period do not wait for a new instance to start. Capping instances at one limits scale, and cutting memory can slow the service down.

questions.stem: A support assistant built on a Gemini model sometimes invents product details. Which change most reduces this?
options: Remove the system instructions so the model is less limited
Increase the model's maximum output length for each answer
Ground answers in the retrieved product docs
Ask users to rate answers
questions.explanation: Grounding, such as retrieval-augmented generation over the product documentation, gives the model the facts to answer from and so reduces invented details. Longer outputs, ratings or fewer instructions do not supply the missing facts.

questions.stem: A public sector customer needs a Google Cloud environment with enforced data location, personnel access controls and other controls for a specific compliance regime. Which product is designed for this?
options: Assured Workloads
Cloud Deploy
Migration Center
Memorystore for Redis
questions.explanation: Assured Workloads creates folders configured for a compliance regime, applying controls such as data residency, restrictions on which products can be used and support personnel limits. Cloud Deploy releases software, and Migration Center assesses migrations.

questions.stem: Which test checks that separate components, such as an API and its database, work correctly together?
options: A static spelling check
An integration test
A soak load test
A unit test
questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise components together, such as a service writing to and reading from its real database. Unit tests check one small piece in isolation, and load tests measure behavior under heavy traffic.

questions.stem: Which kind of test is the fastest and is usually run on every commit?
options: DR drills
Penetration tests
Unit tests
Full load tests
questions.explanation: Unit tests check small pieces of code in isolation and run in seconds, so pipelines run them on every commit. Load tests, DR drills and penetration tests are slower and run less often.

questions.stem: Which practice lets a team turn a new feature off in production without redeploying code?
options: A lifecycle rule
A feature flag
A cold standby
A larger machine type
questions.explanation: Feature flags separate deployment from release: code ships turned off and the feature can be switched on or off at runtime, which makes rollback of a feature instant. The other options are DR, sizing and storage features.

questions.stem: An architect wants help drafting a first architecture for a new workload and later investigating a spike in errors, from inside the Google Cloud console. Which tool is designed for this?
options: Gemini Cloud Assist
Looker Studio reports
Cloud Shell Editor
Migration Center
questions.explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist is an AI assistant in Google Cloud that helps design, deploy, troubleshoot and optimize applications, for example by proposing an architecture or investigating an issue. Cloud Shell Editor is an IDE, Migration Center assesses migrations, and Looker Studio builds reports.

questions.stem: A company wants to try several foundation models, both Google's and open models, and compare them before building an application. Where should the team start?
options: BigQuery's public datasets catalog
Model Garden in Agent Platform
The Vision API page
Cloud Storage's Autoclass settings
questions.explanation: Model Garden is the catalog of first-party, third-party and open models in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), where teams can discover, test, tune and deploy them. The Vision API is one pre-trained model for images, not a place to compare models.

questions.stem: A company running workloads in Google Cloud VMware Engine wants those VMs to reach Compute Engine VMs in its VPC network privately. What connects them?
options: Cloud CDN placed between the two environments for every request
Public IP addresses on every VMware VM and every Compute Engine VM
A Cloud Storage bucket shared by both environments for messages
Private connection between the VMware Engine network and the VPC
questions.explanation: VMware Engine private clouds connect to customer VPC networks through private connections (private services access), so the two environments route traffic over internal addresses. Public IPs expose both sides, and a bucket or CDN is not a network path.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an AI agent from a simple chatbot in Google's descriptions of agentic AI?
options: An agent plans steps and uses tools to act
An agent is a person who reviews chatbot answers
An agent never calls APIs or other systems
An agent only answers questions from a fixed FAQ list
questions.explanation: Agentic AI systems reason about a goal, plan steps and act through tools and APIs, such as looking up an order and issuing a refund, often with a human approving key actions. A chatbot that answers from a fixed list cannot take actions.

questions.stem: An organization wants to prevent any VM in its production folder from being created with an external IP address. What should it apply?
options: A VPC firewall rule that blocks egress to the internet for every VM
An IAM role that lets only admins see VM network settings
An organization policy on VM external IPs for that folder
A label on the folder that says external IPs are not allowed
questions.explanation: The organization policy constraint for VM external IP access, set on the production folder, stops VMs there from getting external IPs, including in new projects. Firewall rules filter traffic but do not stop an IP being assigned, and labels are not enforced.

questions.stem: A batch analytics team's BigQuery bill swings sharply month to month, and finance wants predictable spend. Which option should the architect evaluate?
options: Moving the data into Cloud SQL for every query
Capacity-based pricing with slot reservations
Running each query twice to check the results
Exporting all tables to Archive storage daily
questions.explanation: BigQuery offers on-demand pricing by bytes processed and capacity-based pricing through slot reservations; a reservation makes cost predictable for steady analytics use. Cloud SQL is not built for large analytics, and duplicating queries or exporting data raises cost.

questions.stem: A server-side application running on Compute Engine must call Google Cloud APIs. How should it authenticate?
options: With a developer's user password stored in an environment variable
With a key baked into the image
With an API key copied from the console into the application's code
As the VM's service account, through default credentials
questions.explanation: Workloads on Google Cloud should use the identity of an attached service account, which client libraries find automatically through Application Default Credentials, so no secret is stored. API keys identify a project and work for only some APIs, and keys in images or passwords are exposed.

questions.stem: During a major incident, many engineers are working in parallel and nobody knows who decides what. What practice helps most?
options: Stop all communication until the incident has been fully resolved
Wait for the most senior person in the company to arrive and decide
Name an incident commander who coordinates roles and communication
Let every engineer make changes on their own without telling others
questions.explanation: Incident management assigns clear roles, an incident commander who coordinates, people who investigate and someone who communicates, so work is not duplicated and stakeholders stay informed. Uncoordinated changes can make the outage worse.

questions.stem: A finance team worries that moving to Google Cloud will lock it into today's machine sizes. Which property of Compute Engine addresses this most directly?
options: Bigger machines need a new contract
VMs must keep the machine type chosen when first created
Each project can use only one machine family at a time
Machine types can be changed or customized
questions.explanation: A stopped VM can be moved to a different machine type, and custom machine types let teams choose vCPU and memory amounts to fit the workload. Projects can mix machine families freely, and resizing does not need a new contract.

questions.stem: Before cutting over a migrated application, an architect wants confidence it will meet its performance target in Google Cloud. What should the plan include?
options: A promise from the vendor that the software runs on any cloud
Last year's CPU graphs from the source
A single manual login to the new environment by one tester
Load testing the migrated copy at production load
questions.explanation: Workload testing means running the migrated system under realistic load in the target environment and comparing results with the agreed target before cutover. Old graphs, a single login or a vendor promise do not show how the new deployment behaves.

questions.stem: A game server uses UDP and must see each client's original source IP address. Which load balancer should the architect choose?
options: Internal Application Load Balancer
External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Global external Application Load Balancer
Global external proxy Network Load Balancer
questions.explanation: A passthrough Network Load Balancer forwards packets without proxying, so back ends see the client IP, and it supports UDP. Application Load Balancers handle HTTP and HTTPS, and proxy load balancers terminate the connection, so back ends see the proxy instead.

questions.stem: A team's distributed training job on many GPUs is slowed because workers wait on each other to exchange gradients. Which part of the AI Hypercomputer design addresses this?
options: Archive storage for the training data in a distant region
Fewer GPUs per worker
A single Cloud SQL database for all the model weights
Fast networking between the accelerators
questions.explanation: Large training jobs depend on fast interconnect between accelerators so gradient exchange does not stall the workers; the AI Hypercomputer pairs accelerators with high-bandwidth networking and fast storage. Distant cold storage or smaller nodes make the problem worse.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of rotating encryption keys regularly in Cloud KMS?
options: To lower storage costs for encrypted objects
To speed up reads of encrypted data from disk
To limit how much data any single key version protects
To make old data unreadable as soon as a new key exists
questions.explanation: Rotation creates new key versions for new encryption, which limits the amount of data protected by one version and the impact if it is compromised. Old versions stay available to decrypt older data unless they are disabled or destroyed, and rotation does not change cost or speed.

questions.stem: An architecture review must choose between two managed databases. Which two practices make the decision sound and easy to revisit? (Choose two.)
options: Record the decision, its reasons and trade-offs in a decision record
Score both options against agreed requirements and constraints
Choose the product that the newest team member has used before
Pick whichever option has the most marketing material online
Decide quickly in a chat thread and keep no written record of it
questions.explanation: Comparing options against the stated functional and non-functional requirements, and recording the choice and its trade-offs in an architecture decision record, makes the decision transparent and easy to review when needs change.

questions.stem: Why do architects prefer infrastructure as code over console clicks for production environments?
options: It stops resources from ever failing
It makes every resource free of charge
It removes the need to plan any architecture
Changes are versioned, reviewed and repeatable
questions.explanation: Code in version control gives a history of every change, lets changes be reviewed before they apply, and recreates environments the same way each time. It does not remove the need for design, cost or reliability work.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a load test in production readiness?
options: To check that the code compiles without any errors
To list the IAM roles granted on the project
To find limits under expected and peak traffic
To estimate next year's office rent and travel
questions.explanation: Load tests measure how the system behaves under realistic and peak traffic, revealing limits in quotas, databases and scaling before users find them. Compiling code and listing IAM roles are separate checks.

questions.stem: A stateful web application uses local disk for user sessions, so it cannot run behind a load balancer on more than one VM. Which two changes make it ready for a highly available, autoscaled design? (Choose two.)
options: Keep uploaded files in Cloud Storage rather than on local disk
Increase the boot disk size of the single VM
Store sessions in Memorystore instead of on the VM
Schedule a weekly reboot of the VM to clear memory
Use a static external IP address for the VM
questions.explanation: Moving state off the VM, sessions to a shared cache and files to object storage, makes instances interchangeable so a managed instance group can add, remove or replace them. A bigger disk, static IP or reboot schedule leave the single point of failure in place.

questions.stem: An enterprise will connect 40 VPC networks, two data centers and a branch network, and wants a simpler design than a mesh of peerings and tunnels. Which two choices help? (Choose two.)
options: One large /8 subnet reused in every VPC network
Network Connectivity Center as a hub for the spokes
A public IP on each VM so routing is not needed
Peering every VPC with every other VPC directly
Non-overlapping IP ranges planned across all sites
questions.explanation: Network Connectivity Center provides a hub-and-spoke model for VPCs and hybrid connections, and planning non-overlapping address space up front avoids routing conflicts. A full mesh of peerings grows quickly and is not transitive, and reusing the same range everywhere makes routing impossible.

questions.stem: A storage bucket holds files that should be readable only by one application's service account, with no public access ever possible. Which two settings support this? (Choose two.)
options: Grant roles/storage.objectViewer to that service account only
Grant roles/storage.admin to allUsers for easier testing
Store the service account's key file in the bucket itself
Use per-object ACLs that each developer sets by hand
Enforce public access prevention on the bucket
questions.explanation: Public access prevention blocks any grant to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers, and a read-only role on that one service account follows least privilege. Uniform bucket-level access is preferred over per-object ACLs, and a key file in the bucket is a credential leak.

questions.stem: A company will soon launch a public generative AI assistant. Which two pre-launch steps most reduce the risk of harmful or wrong answers? (Choose two.)
options: Raise the temperature so that answers sound more natural
Red-team the assistant with adversarial and off-topic prompts
Skip testing because the foundation model is already tuned
Evaluate answers on a test set for quality, groundedness and safety
Hide from users that the answers come from an AI system
questions.explanation: Systematic evaluation on representative questions measures quality, groundedness and safety, and red-teaming with adversarial prompts finds jailbreaks and failure modes before users do. Higher temperature adds variability, and hiding AI use or skipping tests adds risk.

questions.stem: A clinic's analytics team wants to study visit patterns in BigQuery without seeing names or record numbers. Which two measures help? (Choose two.)
options: Use column-level access control on any remaining sensitive columns
De-identify identifiers with Sensitive Data Protection before loading
Copy the raw records to a public dataset for easier sharing
Grant the analysts Owner on the project holding the raw data
Email exports of the raw tables to the analysts each week
questions.explanation: De-identifying names and record numbers with masking or tokenization keeps direct identifiers out of the analysis, and BigQuery column-level security with policy tags restricts any sensitive columns that remain. Public datasets, Owner access and emailed exports expose the raw data.

questions.stem: Recommender reports that several VMs use under 10% of their CPU for weeks. What is the usual action?
options: Add more vCPUs so the usage percentage looks healthier
Resize them smaller after checking their peaks
Move them to sole-tenant nodes to isolate them
Ignore it, since idle CPUs cost nothing in the cloud
questions.explanation: Rightsizing recommendations from Recommender suggest smaller machine types for underused VMs; after checking peaks and memory, resizing cuts cost. Idle capacity is still billed.

questions.stem: A development team will deploy its first service on Google Cloud and asks the architect what to set up before the first release. Which two items should come first? (Choose two.)
options: A manual deploy by copying files to each VM
Monitoring and alerting on the service's key SLOs
A CI/CD pipeline that builds, tests and deploys the service
Owner access for every developer in production
Logging turned off to keep the first bill small
questions.explanation: A pipeline makes releases repeatable and safe, and monitoring with alerts on SLOs shows whether the service works once users arrive. Broad Owner access, manual copying and disabled logging all add risk.

questions.stem: A team is defining the "golden signals" to monitor for a user-facing web service. Which two belong on that list? (Choose two.)
options: Latency of requests
Size of the source code repository
Error rate of requests
Color scheme of the website
Number of developers on the team
questions.explanation: The four golden signals from Google's SRE practice are latency, traffic, errors and saturation. They describe what users experience and how close the system is to its limits; team size and code size do not.

questions.stem: A development environment runs on VMs that are used only during office hours. What is the simplest way to cut its compute cost?
options: Buy a three-year committed use discount for them
Move them to sole-tenant nodes in the same zone
Add a second region to spread the load evenly
Schedule the VMs to stop outside office hours
questions.explanation: Stopped VMs do not incur compute charges, so an instance schedule that stops them at night and on weekends removes most of the cost. A commitment charges for the capacity whether it runs or not, and sole tenancy or a second region add cost.

questions.stem: An existing PostgreSQL application needs higher transaction throughput and fast analytical queries on live data, with minimal code change. Which managed database should the architect evaluate?
options: Firestore in Native mode
Memorystore for Redis
Bigtable with a single cluster
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
questions.explanation: AlloyDB is a PostgreSQL-compatible managed database built for demanding transactional workloads, with a columnar engine that speeds up analytical queries. Firestore and Bigtable are NoSQL and would need a rewrite, and Memorystore is an in-memory cache.

questions.stem: A company must copy 200 TB of objects from another cloud provider's object storage into Cloud Storage, then sync changes daily for a month. Which service fits?
options: Database Migration Service
Cloud Deploy
Transfer Appliance
Storage Transfer Service
questions.explanation: Storage Transfer Service moves data online from other clouds, HTTP sources and on-premises file systems into Cloud Storage, and can run scheduled incremental transfers. Transfer Appliance is for offline bulk moves, and Database Migration Service moves databases.

questions.stem: A news company wants to find the times in its video archive where specific objects and logos appear, without training a model. Which API fits?
options: Video Intelligence API
Cloud Natural Language API
Speech-to-Text
Document AI
questions.explanation: The Video Intelligence API detects objects, logos, shot changes and more in stored video. The Natural Language API analyzes text, Speech-to-Text transcribes audio, and Document AI extracts data from documents.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the zero trust model that Google's BeyondCorp approach is based on?
options: Every request is checked by identity and context
Access is granted by IP address alone, since addresses cannot be faked
Anything inside the corporate network is trusted without further checks
Users are trusted after a yearly sign-in
questions.explanation: Zero trust removes the idea of a trusted internal network: each request is authenticated and authorized using the user's identity, the device's state and other context. Network location or an old sign-in is not enough.

questions.stem: A security team keeps blocking a migration late in each phase with new requirements. What would most likely prevent this?
options: Leave security out of planning so that the project can move faster
Involve security at design and agree requirements early
Ask the sponsor to overrule the security team at every objection
Hide the design until cutover
questions.explanation: Involving key stakeholders such as security early lets their requirements shape the design instead of surfacing as late blockers. Excluding, overruling or hiding work from them creates conflict and risk.

questions.stem: Which statement about Cloud Shell is accurate?
options: A paid VM that keeps running with its own external IP
A way to skip IAM permissions on the projects it manages
A tool that runs only Kubernetes commands, without gcloud
A browser terminal with tools and a persistent home folder
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell gives a temporary VM in the browser with the gcloud CLI, kubectl, Terraform and editors preinstalled, plus a small persistent home directory that survives sessions. Commands run in it still need the user's IAM permissions.

questions.stem: After several incidents with the same root cause, what should the team do so the problem stops recurring?
options: Close each incident quickly and treat them as unrelated
Track it as a problem and fix the cause
Stop logging that service so that the alerts go away
Reapply the workaround each time
questions.explanation: Problem management looks across incidents for a shared cause and fixes it, for example with code, configuration or capacity changes. Treating repeats as unrelated or relying on workarounds keeps the incidents coming.
